summary: The study investigates the atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) of CdTe and MnTe, focusing on the growth mechanisms, self-regulated growth rates, and surface reconstructions. The ALE process for CdTe shows a self-regulated growth rate of 0.5 monolayers per cycle at temperatures between 260 and 290 °C, while MnTe does not exhibit self-regulation due to all Mn atoms being incorporated. The study also examines the structural quality of the resulting layers using RHEED, XRD, and TEM.
evidence: The ALE CdTe autoregulated growth rate at 0.5 monolayer/cycle (in the substrate temperature domain between 260 and 290 °C) is accounted for on the basis of an atomic model which relies on the alternating c(2 32) Cd and (231) Te surface reconstructions during the ALE cycle. For MnTe, all deposited Mn atoms are incorporated so that no autoregulated growth can be achieved.
